allowed_dependency_manifest.content: Let n, k, l ∈ Z with 0 ≤ k, l ≤ n. Define R(q) = [n choose k]_q / [n choose l]_q in the natural rational-function setting for Gaussian q-binomial coefficients. If R(q) lies in a polynomial ring in q (i.e., R(q) has only finitely many nonnegative powers of q with coefficients in the relevant coefficient ring), then when written as R(q) = Σ_i c_i q^i, every coefficient c_i satisfies c_i ≥ 0.

forbidden_claims.statement_nl: Let [n choose k]_q denote the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient. Prove that for all integers n, k, l with 0 ≤ k, l ≤ n, if [n choose k]_q / [n choose l]_q is a polynomial in q, then that polynomial has only nonnegative coefficients.

payload.role_in_assembly: Converts the reduced quotient into the consecutive-interval product form needed for the commutative-algebra model.

domain_restrictions: R(q) must be well-defined as a formal expression: [n choose l]_q ≠ 0 and division is interpreted in the ambient field/ring where Gaussian coefficients live (typically Q(q) or a localization of Z[q])
the premise “is a polynomial in q” means R(q) has no negative powers of q (i.e., R(q) ∈ coefficient_ring[q] for some coefficient ring)

payload.statement_nl: For integers n, a, b with 0 <= b <= a <= n/2, let d := a - b, A := n - a, and B := b. Define [n choose t]_q := prod_{i=1}^t (1 - q^(n-t+i)) / (1 - q^i), with the empty product equal to 1 when t = 0. Then [n choose a]_q / [n choose b]_q = prod_{i=1}^d (1 - q^(A+i)) / (1 - q^(B+i)), where the product is 1 if d = 0.

result_payload.proof_nl:
Since 0 <= b <= a <= n/2, we have d = a - b >= 0 and a = b + d. Also n - a >= a >= 0, so for every index that appears below, the exponents n-a+i, n-b+i, i, and b+i are positive integers. Hence all factors 1 - q^m that occur are nonzero polynomials, and the manipulations below are valid in the ambient field of rational functions in q.

By the definition of the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient,
[n choose a]_q / [n choose b]_q
= (prod_{i=1}^a ((1 - q^(n-a+i))/(1 - q^i))) / (prod_{i=1}^b ((1 - q^(n-b+i))/(1 - q^i)))
= ((prod_{i=1}^a (1 - q^(n-a+i))) (prod_{i=1}^b (1 - q^i))) / ((prod_{i=1}^a (1 - q^i)) (prod_{i=1}^b (1 - q^(n-b+i)))).

Now split the length-a products using a = b + d.
First,
prod_{i=1}^a (1 - q^(n-a+i))
= (prod_{i=1}^d (1 - q^(n-a+i))) (prod_{i=d+1}^{d+b} (1 - q^(n-a+i)))
= (prod_{i=1}^d (1 - q^(n-a+i))) (prod_{j=1}^b (1 - q^(n-a+d+j)))
= (prod_{i=1}^d (1 - q^(n-a+i))) (prod_{j=1}^b (1 - q^(n-b+j))),
where in the middle step we reindexed by j = i - d.

Second,
prod_{i=1}^a (1 - q^i)
= (prod_{i=1}^b (1 - q^i)) (prod_{j=1}^d (1 - q^(b+j))).

Substituting these two decompositions into the previous fraction gives
[n choose a]_q / [n choose b]_q
= ((prod_{i=1}^d (1 - q^(n-a+i))) (prod_{j=1}^b (1 - q^(n-b+j))) (prod_{i=1}^b (1 - q^i)))
  / ((prod_{i=1}^b (1 - q^i)) (prod_{j=1}^d (1 - q^(b+j))) (prod_{j=1}^b (1 - q^(n-b+j)))).

The identical b-factor products cancel, so
[n choose a]_q / [n choose b]_q
= (prod_{i=1}^d (1 - q^(n-a+i))) / (prod_{i=1}^d (1 - q^(b+i)))
= prod_{i=1}^d ((1 - q^(n-a+i))/(1 - q^(b+i))).

Finally, since A = n - a and B = b, this is exactly
prod_{i=1}^d ((1 - q^(A+i))/(1 - q^(B+i))).

If d = 0, then these are empty products, hence equal to 1, so the same identity also covers the case a = b. Therefore
[n choose a]_q / [n choose b]_q = prod_{i=1}^d ((1 - q^(A+i))/(1 - q^(B+i))),
with the right-hand side equal to 1 when d = 0, as claimed.
result_payload.proof_summary: Expand both Gaussian q-binomial coefficients from the definition, use a = b + d to split the length-a numerator and denominator products into a d-part and a b-part, then cancel the common b-part factors. The remaining factors are exactly prod_{i=1}^d ((1-q^(A+i))/(1-q^(B+i))).
